args.message:
Use ROUND_HALF_EVEN in round_money per FIN-212

round_money claimed banker's rounding in its docstring but was actually
using ROUND_HALF_UP. Switch to ROUND_HALF_EVEN so ties round to the
nearest even cent, as expected by tests/test_money.py and FIN-212.

args.head: fix/money-rounding-half-even
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding, but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` despite its docstring claiming `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` (per FIN-212).

- Changed the rounding mode in `round_money` from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`.
- No behavioral changes other than the rounding mode: ties (e.g. `2.675`, `2.665`) now round to the nearest even cent (`2.68`, `2.66`).

## CI
Run `ci-0001` on `08d3cd5986` passed.

Reviewer: @alex

trace.final:
Done. Summary of what I did:

1. **Diagnosed the bug**: `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP` in `round_money` even though the docstring (and FIN-212) called for banker's rounding — this caused `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` to fail.
2. **Created branch** `fix/money-rounding-half-even` off main and committed a one-line fix: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in the `quantize` call.
3. **Ran CI** on the branch (`ci-0001`) — it **passed**.
4. **Opened PR #101** against main with alex as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The fix makes ties round to the nearest even cent (`2.675 → 2.68`, `2.665 → 2.66`), matching the test expectations. I did not merge — that requires code-owner approval per policy.
